alex_customer: Hi — our March 2 invoice shows a big jump for streaming calls. Dashboard shows ~120k tokens for the session, invoice charged ~360k. This was from live users cancelling mid-generation. Can you investigate?
jordan_support: Sorry about that — can you share a request_id or time window? Did the client send an explicit cancel or just close the SSE connection?
alex_customer: request_id=rc_20240302_87a1c. Time window 2024-03-02 15:32-15:50 UTC. Client does a `CTRL-C` in the browser (EventSource close). No explicit cancel HTTP body.
liam_eng: Thanks — likely related to how we account partial generations when streams disconnect. Can you paste the client-side sequence of events (approx)? Also any server logs around that req id.
alex_customer: Repro steps: 1) curl to start SSE: `curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://api.redwood.example/v1/respond?stream=true -d '{"prompt":"..."}'` 2) after ~3s hit ctrl-c. 3) Dashboard session shows 49 tokens. Invoice shows 147 tokens.
jordan_support: Pushing this to eng to check meter event flow and dedup. @liam_eng can you look at streaming meter events for rc_20240302_87a1c?
liam_eng: Pulling logs now. I see two meter events for that session: `stream_chunk: tokens=12, session_id=sess_9, offset=0` then `stream_chunk: tokens=37, session_id=sess_9, offset=12`, then an `session_abort: reason=client_disconnect, session_id=sess_9, abort_tokens=49` and finally a `session_finalize: session_id=sess_9, final_tokens=98`. Looks like both abort and finalize were credited.
maya_sre: That pattern explains ~147=49+98. Need to know why finalize emitted after abort. Could be race between generator finalizer (background flush) and abort handler.
liam_eng: Repro locally with a fast cancel — got same sequence. The generator pipeline flush still emits a `finalize` after the abort if the KV cache flush happens.
jordan_support: Billing impact: do we double-count in invoices when both events present? @billing_bot / billing team?
billing_bot: Invoice automation sums token events by session_id and event_type. Currently we add up `chunk_tokens` + `abort_tokens` + `final_tokens`. There's no dedupe rule for `session_id` duplicate credit. We can pause invoicing for the affected session ids if engineering confirms duplication.
liam_eng: Short-term mitigation: add a rule in billing pipeline to prefer `finalize` over `abort` (or vice versa) when both exist for the same session_id within a 5s window. Longer fix: ensure abort handler cancels any pending finalizer event emission.
maya_sre: Agree. Also add an idempotency token to finalizer events (`final_event_id`) so billing can dedupe.
jordan_support: Action items: 1) Eng to propose patch for server finalizer (liam). 2) Billing to run hold/adjust for invoices touching session_id=sess_9 and rc_20240302_87a1c (billing). 3) Support to notify customer with ETA.
liam_eng: I'll open a PR for canceling finalizer and add a temporary billing-safe flag. Quick SQL to find affected sessions: `SELECT session_id, SUM(chunk_tokens)+SUM(abort_tokens)+SUM(final_tokens) as billed, MAX(dashboard_tokens) FROM meter_events WHERE timestamp BETWEEN '2024-03-02' AND '2024-03-03' GROUP BY session_id HAVING billed > MAX(dashboard_tokens)*2;`
billing_bot: Running a scan for that day now. Found ~24 sessions matching pattern. Holding invoice lines for those session_ids and flagging for adjustment.
alex_customer: Thanks — appreciate the quick triage. Please keep me posted; we'll hold payment on disputed line items until resolved.
jordan_support: Will send status update in 2 hours. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
liam_eng: FYI for reproducible test: here's a minimal repro script (node):

const es = new EventSource(url);
es.onmessage = m => console.log(m.data);
setTimeout(() => { es.close(); }, 2500);

Run against a dev instance and watch meter_events stream.
maya_sre: I'll add an alert to catch large finalization-after-abort patterns and track rollbacks.
jordan_support: Marking this thread as escalated -> eng-billing-sync. I'll create the internal ticket with the logs.
